nodes.strategy: M^(a,b) is the permutation representation on tabloids; tabloids of shape (a,b) are in equivariant bijection with the coset space S_(a+b)/(S_a x S_b). Induction of the trivial representation along an injective homomorphism into a finite group is the permutation representation on cosets. Build the equivariant bijection explicitly and transport it with FDRep.ofMulActionEquiv, which the module already provides.

nodes.strategy: Pure combinatorics, no representation theory. Write r = min k (n-k). For the weight (n-r, r) a semistandard tableau has only the entries 0 and 1; strict columns put at most one 0 above one 1 in each column, and weak rows force row 0 to be 0^a 1^b and row 1 to be all 1s. Hence K_(shape,(n-r,r)) = 1 when shape = (n-i, i) with i <= r and 0 otherwise. Recover i from a shape as shape.rowLen 1 to define the forward map, and send i to the unique tableau of shape (n-i, i) for the inverse.

Immediate from the construction of twoRowKostkaIndexEquiv once its forward map is defined as shape.rowLen 1, because twoRowShape n k hk i is twoRowPartition n i and a two-row shape is determined by its second row length.

Pure combinatorics. Introduce the first-column hook lengths l_i = mu.rowLen i + (m - 1 - i) for a row bound m. Prove that the hook lengths in row i are exactly {1,...,l_i} minus {l_i - l_j : j > i}, giving hookProduct = prod l_i! / prod_(i<j) (l_i - l_j). Prove independently that the number of standard tableaux satisfies the corner recursion f(mu) = sum over corners of f(mu - c), and that n! * prod (l_i - l_j) / prod l_i! satisfies the same recursion, which reduces to a Vandermonde-style polynomial identity. Conclude by induction on n.

The project already proves symmetricGroup_character_inv, that every symmetric-group character is inversion invariant, from Equiv.Perm.cycleType_inv. Combining that with the theorem that finite-dimensional complex representations of a finite group with equal characters are isomorphic gives the isomorphism. nodes.strategy: The standard basis theorem: the polytabloids e_t for standard t form a basis of S^mu. Proved from Garnir relations and the straightening algorithm on the polytabloid module. This is the classical resolution of the apparent circularity with the branching rule: Sagan establishes the standard basis theorem first and uses it to prove branching, so the edge runs from here to spechtModule_branching and not back.

Define the dominance order on Young diagrams and prove that a nonzero homomorphism S^lambda -> M^mu forces lambda to dominate mu. Since S^mu embeds in M^mu, an isomorphism S^lambda = S^mu gives dominance both ways, hence equality. The converse direction is definitional.

Completeness by counting. The Specht modules are pairwise non-isomorphic simples indexed by YoungDiagramOfSize n. Over C the number of isomorphism classes of simple representations of a finite group equals the number of conjugacy classes, and conjugacy classes of Equiv.Perm (Fin n) are classified by cycle type, hence by partitions of n. A bijection YoungDiagramOfSize n = Nat.Partition n then forces the Specht list to be exhaustive.

apparent_cycles_resolved.problem: dim S^mu = number of standard tableaux follows quickly from the branching rule, while the classical proof of the branching rule uses the standard basis.
apparent_cycles_resolved.resolution: Break it at the common lower-level construction: the Garnir relations and the straightening algorithm on the polytabloid module prove the standard basis theorem directly from the layer-1 construction, with no branching input. The graph therefore carries only the edge exists_spechtTableauBasis -> spechtModule_branching.

apparent_cycles_resolved.problem: completeness of the Specht list can be argued from branching by induction, which would make the classification depend on results that themselves need the classification.
apparent_cycles_resolved.resolution: Prove completeness by the independent count of conjugacy classes of Equiv.Perm (Fin n) against partitions of n, so nothing in layers 2 to 4 uses branching.

apparent_cycles_resolved.problem: Rosmanis's reduction and the Littlewood-Richardson rule both talk about restrict-then-induce multiplicities.
apparent_cycles_resolved.resolution: Littlewood-Richardson is proved from the semistandard basis and Young's rule; the Rosmanis reduction consumes it. Edges run one way only.

source_pack_issues.issue: The bundled file is the 22-page arXiv:1401.3826v3 paper 'Quantum Adversary Lower Bound for Element Distinctness with Small Range', not the 181-page thesis that .claude/reference-pdfs/README.md describes. It contains no Section 1.4.2 and no Lemma 1.12.
source_pack_issues.resolution: Both cited passages were verified against a correct copy of the thesis found elsewhere on this machine. Page references recorded here are for the real thesis (pdf page = printed page + 13). The Lean docstrings need no change; the reference pack does.

source_pack_issues.issue: The bundled copy is the 10 January 2011 draft, which uses flat per-chapter numbering (Theorem 3.1, Corollary 3.7, Theorem 4.25). The Lean docstrings cite the published edition's numbering (4.1.1, 4.2.4, 4.5.4, 3.10.2), which does not resolve in this file.
source_pack_issues.resolution: Mapping recorded per node: 4.1.1(ii) is Theorem 3.1(ii) p.33; 4.2.4 is Corollary 3.7 p.35; 3.10.2 (products) is Theorem 4.25 p.54; there is no analogue of 4.5.4, only an unnumbered Peter-Weyl remark on p.68. Docstrings are left untouched because they cite the published edition correctly.

source_pack_issues.issue: Pieri is never named in Sagan 2e; a full-text search over all 254 pages returns zero hits, and there is no horizontal-strip or vertical-strip exercise in Section 4.11.
source_pack_issues.resolution: Both Pieri nodes are derived as the one-row and one-column specialisations of Theorem 4.9.4, which is exactly how the dependency graph already routes them.

source_pack_issues.issue: Rosmanis Lemma 1.12 is stated without proof. The thesis explicitly declines to introduce the determinantal form of the irreducibles or the general Littlewood-Richardson rule, which is what a proof would need.
source_pack_issues.resolution: This target has no proof in its cited source, so it must be proved here from the Littlewood-Richardson rule and the branching rule. The thesis's Corollary 1.13, a special case, is proved from the branching rule and is the model to follow. Recorded as the highest-risk node.
